verdict: Coinbase rode the post-election crypto rally to its biggest quarter yet: revenue jumped 88% from Q3 to $2.27B as trading surged, and it kept $1.29B as profit — helped by a $476M paper gain on the crypto it holds as an investment.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago — and +88% from Q3 as crypto rallied

segments.name: Transaction revenue
segments.note: Fees from crypto trading — consumer $1,347M, institutional $141M, other $68M. Trading volume hit $439B as crypto prices and volatility surged after the US election.

segments.name: Subscription and services
segments.note: Steadier income: stablecoin revenue $226M, blockchain rewards $215M, interest and finance fees $66M, custody fees $43M and other services $91M.

segments.note: Interest earned on Coinbase's own corporate cash.

opex.note: Building the platform — engineering and product.

opex.note: Running the company — legal, compliance and the back office.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Advertising, USDC rewards and winning customers — more than double a year ago as Coinbase marketed into the crypto rally.

otherDetail: A $476M gain on crypto Coinbase holds as an investment — a paper gain as prices rose — plus $7M of other income and $37M of net operating gains Coinbase reports inside its expense lines (a $16M gain on crypto held for operations and $21M of other operating income), less $21M of interest expense: a net $499M.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Trading exploded after the election
takeaways.text: Trading volume reached $439B in the quarter, and transaction revenue rose 172% from Q3 to $1.56B as crypto prices and volatility surged in November and December. Trading is still the engine: it brought in 68 cents of every revenue dollar.

takeaways.title: A record profit
takeaways.text: Net income was $1.29B, nearly five times a year ago. About $476M of it was a paper gain on crypto Coinbase holds as an investment — real only if prices hold — but the core business was strongly profitable on its own, with $1.03B of reported operating income.

takeaways.title: The steady side kept growing too
takeaways.text: Subscription and services revenue — stablecoins, staking rewards, custody — rose 15% from Q3 to $641M. It is smaller than trading but far less dependent on market mood swings.

oneTimers: A $476M pre-tax gain on crypto assets held for investment — unrealized, and it reverses if crypto prices fall.

$37M of net operating gains (crypto held for operations, and other operating income) that Coinbase reports inside its expense lines; the chart shows them in the other-income step — see the note under the chart.
footerNote: Coinbase reports no gross-profit line; 'Transaction expense' — the direct cost of processing trades — is shown as cost of revenue. Coinbase also reports two gain lines inside operating expenses (a $16M gain on crypto held for operations and $20M of other operating income — $37M in total); the chart shows that $37M in the 'other income' step instead, so the chart's operating profit is $998M rather than the reported $1,034M — net income is unchanged. Segment revenue is exact from Coinbase's Form 10-K (full year) less its Q3 2024 Form 10-Q (nine months). Figures are from Coinbase's Q4 2024 shareholder letter (Exhibit 99.1) and Form 10-K.
